fact: The National Payments Council's March 2020 e-payment services regulation, issued under the Central Bank of Libya, has a consumer protection chapter requiring e-payment and mobile-wallet providers to give clear written service information, non-misleading advertising and call-centre support.

The regulation requires provider contracts to give contact details for the provider's complaints unit and the relevant Central Bank of Libya unit, where a complaint is unresolved or the customer is dissatisfied, and to let customers complain free of charge.
The Central Bank of Libya's LYPay instant payment website includes a platform for submitting complaints and inquiries.
